text: In World War Two, Britain built a giant wheel of explosives, strapped rockets to it, and hoped it would roll in a straight line. The Great Panjandrum. Two wheels, three metres tall, with nearly two tonnes of explosive in the middle. Rockets on the rims would spin it up a beach and into enemy defences. If one rocket fails, the push is lopsided. The wheel turns toward the side that's still pushing. At the final trial, the rockets started flying off. It swerved straight at the cameraman. Officers dived for cover behind the pebbles. It was never used in the war. Dave volunteered to steer.
